title: Arogya: Interpretable Joint-Angle Templates for Camera-Based Assessment of Home Rehabilitation Exercises
content: Home exercise programmes are central to rehabilitation, but patients mostly perform them unsupervised, and clinicians learn little about how the exercises were actually done. We present Arogya, a camera-only home rehabilitation system in which each exercise is described by a template of named joint-angle ranges that a physiotherapist can read and adjust for an individual patient. A repetition is scored by how far its measured angles fall outside those ranges, so every warning refers to a specific joint and a specific size of deviation. We evaluated the measurement and decision stages on the public REHAB24-6 dataset (10 participants, six exercises, 1,057 labelled repetitions), using MediaPipe Pose on ordinary RGB video and synchronised optical motion capture as the reference. Repetition-level trunk, hip and knee angles agreed with motion capture with mean absolute errors of 5.1°, 8.9° and 10.8° (r = 0.88–0.94). Elbow angles were less reliable (20.9°), and a camera at half-profile gave the best agreement for most angles. In leave-one-subject-out evaluation, the templates detected incorrect repetitions with a mean balanced accuracy of 0.58 (AUC 0.62). The same templates reached 0.60 on motion-capture angles, and a random forest trained on the same features reached 0.63. Pose estimation and template evaluation together ran at 25 frames per second on four CPU cores. For this task a single camera comes close to motion capture; the main limitation is what joint-angle extremes can express. We discuss what this implies for per-patient, clinician-set criteria.
